# Niger

Wealth gradients in fertility and mortality: the values for an OG-Core calibration, followed by the estimates they are based on. Terms are defined in the [glossary](../glossary.md).

## Values for OG-Core

| OG-Core input | Wealth gradient | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `fert_gradient` | −0.30, by age as below | DHS 2021, TFR, plus [age offsets](../methods/fertility-by-age.md) |
| `infmort_gradient` | −0.21 | DHS 2012, infant mortality rate |
| `mort_gradient` | 2.96 − 0.431 × ln(GDP per capita, PPP) | [general gradient](../methods/general-gradient.md), GDP per capita in constant 2021 international $; for example −0.32 at $2,000 and −1.01 at $10,000, each with a 95% prediction interval of about ±0.7 |
| `imm_pctiles` | not provided | — |

Values are [wealth gradients](../glossary.md#wealth-gradient). Before they are passed to OG-Core, each is divided by 100 × (1 − p), where p is OG-Core's rate at that age ([details](../methods/ogcore-units.md)).

**Fertility gradient by age of mother** (`fert_gradient`; ages below 15 use the 15–19 value, ages 50 and above the 45–49 value):

| 15–19 | 20–24 | 25–29 | 30–34 | 35–39 | 40–44 | 45–49 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| −1.08 | −0.40 | −0.09 | 0.03 | −0.21 | −0.69 | −1.28 |

**Adult and child mortality gradient by age** (`mort_gradient`; ages 15–59: the general-gradient value for this country plus the pooled offset for each band ([age pattern](../methods/general-gradient.md#age-pattern)); ages 5–14 use the 15–29 value; ages 60–74 fall in a straight line from the 45–59 value to 0 at age 75; ages 75 and above, and OG-Core's final age, use 0):

| 1–4 | 5–14 | 15–29 | 30–44 | 45–59 | 60–74 | 75+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| −0.29 (DHS 2012) | value − 0.39 | value − 0.39 | value − 0.16 | value + 0.20 | the 45–59 value at 60, falling to 0 at 75 | 0 |

Ages 1–4 use the country's own gradient in child mortality at ages 1–4 (DHS), or, where there is none, its under-five gradient plus a pooled offset ([details](../methods/general-gradient.md#age-pattern)). Infant mortality (age 0) is `infmort_gradient`, above.

## Estimates

### Household surveys

Latest Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) or Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) with a complete wealth-quintile breakdown, for each indicator ([`gradient_library_latest.csv`](../../data/gradient_library_latest.csv); earlier surveys in `gradient_library.csv`).

| Indicator | Survey | Lowest | Second | Middle | Fourth | Highest | Low/high ratio | Gradient |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total fertility rate (births per woman) | DHS 2021 | 7.2 | 6.2 | 6.2 | 6.3 | 5.3 | 1.36 | −0.30 |
| Infant mortality rate (per 1,000 live births) | DHS 2012 | 64 | 70 | 67 | 69 | 52 | 1.23 | −0.21 |
| Under-five mortality rate (per 1,000 live births) | DHS 2012 | 144 | 168 | 168 | 164 | 114 | 1.26 | −0.25 |
| Child mortality, ages 1–4 (per 1,000 children aged 1) | DHS 2012 | 86 | 105 | 108 | 102 | 65 | 1.32 | −0.29 |
